Package dev.opencollab.paletter.block

Class BlockHashes

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.block.BlockHashes
public final class BlockHashes extends Object
Block network ids. Palettes always use hashed ids: the runtime id of a block state is the hash of the state (hash(NbtMap)), what the client expects when StartGamePacket#blockNetworkIdsHashed is set (which Palette.applyTo(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.packet.StartGamePacket) does). A state has the same id in every version and in every palette, custom blocks included, so tables and encoded chunks can be shared between client versions.

The exception is a custom state whose hash a state of another block has: like BDS, the palette gives it the next free id (see docs/wire-notes.md), so its id depends on the other blocks of the palette.

Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • hash

      public static int hash(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.nbt.NbtMap state)
      The hashed network id of a block state, as the client computes it: FNV-1a 32 bit over the little endian (not network / varint) NBT of the compound {name, states}, with an empty root name, the state values sorted by key, and no version tag. minecraft:unknown is always -2.

      Sources: Alemiz112's reference implementation (gist 504d0f79feac7ef57eda174b668dd345, used by CloudburstMC / WaterdogPE), and GeyserMC/Geyser#6253. Verified against the network_id BDS writes into its block palette dumps: every state of 26.40, 26.50 and 26.60 matches, e.g. minecraft:air is -604749536.

      Parameters:
      state - a block state as {name, states}; other keys are ignored
      Returns:
      the hash, which is the runtime id of the state
      Since:
      1.0.0
